content.title: Evacuation Day 250th event held in Boston
content.text: Tuesday's ceremony began with a memorial service in St. Augustine's chapel in South Boston, followed by a short procession up to Dorchester Heights for a commemorative program featuring political and community leaders from across the state. NBC Universal, Inc. St. Patrick’s Day is also Evacuation Day in Boston, marking a turning point in the Revolutionary War. Tuesday marks the 250th anniversary of the evacuation of Boston by the British army, and the occasion was marked with a special ceremony and memorial service. Evacuation Day is a legal holiday observed on March 17 in Suffolk County, commemorating the British evacuation of Boston on March 17, 1776. It was the first major victory for George Washington's Continental Army in the American Revolution following an 11-month siege of the city. Tuesday's ceremony began with a memorial service in St. Augustine's chapel in South Boston, followed by a short procession up to Dorchester Heights for a commemorative program featuring political and community leaders from across the state, including Gov. Maura Healey and Boston Mayor Michelle Wu. There were also several reenacting units, including the Lexington Minute Men, the 2nd Massachusetts Regiment, the Henry Knox Color Guard, the Henry Knox Regiment of Artillery and historical assets from Fort Ticonderoga and Saratoga 250.
